Unlike many engineering materials, magnesium powder carries an intrinsic density of only 1.74 g/cm³ for the solid metal, which means even small changes in inter-particle packing have an outsized effect on volumetric efficiency and downstream process stability.

Tap density is measured after mechanically tapping the same cup a fixed number of times (commonly 100 or 500 taps per ISO 3953 or ASTM B527). Tapping collapses inter-particle voids, rearranges bridging particles, and allows the powder column to settle into a denser, more ordered configuration. The resulting tap density for atomized Mg alloy powder generally falls between 0.70 and 1.10 g/cm³.
